module.title: Rigid body dynamics algorithms
module.expensive_path: The recursive tree passes that dominate every robotics pipeline: RNEA's two sweeps for inverse dynamics, ABA's three sweeps for forward dynamics, CRBA plus its sparse Cholesky for the joint-space inertia matrix, and the frame/CoM/centroidal Jacobian assembly. Each call is O(n) to O(nd) on a kinematic tree of tens of joints, so a single evaluation is microseconds, and the cost is the number of evaluations: a model-predictive controller, a trajectory optimizer or a reinforcement-learning rollout evaluates them for thousands to millions of independent (q, v, a) samples per second. That batch-over-samples workload is the acceleration target, and it is exactly what pinocchio's OpenMP pool variants (parallel-rnea, parallel-aba) already approximate on CPU.
module.rationale: These are the Featherstone rigid-body algorithms proper: given a model and a configuration, compute motions, forces, inertia and their aggregates. They share one data layout (Model/Data) and one recursion pattern, they are what every downstream consumer calls first, and they are validated against each other by the upstream tests (nonLinearEffects against RNEA, ABA against the inverse of RNEA, CRBA against the Jacobian-transpose form). Nothing here needs a constraint, a contact, a derivative or a collision geometry.
excluded: analytical derivatives of these same algorithms, which are their own module
anything that introduces a constraint or contact, which is the constrained-dynamics module
Model and Data construction and the parsers that fill them, which are shared infrastructure
hazards: Most upstream tests draw both the model and its operands from an unseeded std::rand stream through Eigen ::Random and randomConfiguration; only matrix.cpp, quaternion.cpp and vector.cpp call srand(0). The upstream sample models are themselves random: buildModels::humanoidRandom draws every joint placement (SE3::Random), every body inertia (Inertia::Random) and every joint limit from the unseeded std::rand stream, so the model, not only the configuration, changes with the standard library. A check must freeze the model as data in ic/ (a serialized Model is the natural form, since the tree ships serialization) rather than rebuild it at run time.
The upstream tests are cross-validation identities between two algorithms in one process, not comparisons against stored references, so each check has to dump the physical quantity itself.
OpenMP pool variants vary the thread schedule; per-sample results are independent, but thread counts must be pinned and never graded.

approval.human_ref: Curator RealZiangLiu, 2026-09-10, verbatim: "approve 1 2 3 4". The numbers are the STOP 1 module list: 1 rigid-body-algorithms, 2 analytical-derivatives, 3 constrained-dynamics, 4 contact-solvers-and-constraint-sets. Modules 5 collision-and-geometry and 6 spatial-algebra-and-joint-models are declined. Licence ruling in the same session, verbatim: "Agree with the lisence, do what's safe" — vendor the pinned tree plus the cmake submodule plus romeo_description and ur_description only (both BSD-3-Clause); exclude talos_data (LGPL-3.0) and cassie_description (no licence stated).
